purpose: An editorial set for telling apart concepts, controlled variants and explainable relations. The basis for a future UX benchmark.

limitations: 96 real frames captured; visual review completed with findings. Full accessibility checks and human studies are not finished yet.
Passports rest on the sources; character and fitness are editorial hypotheses.
Mass schematics do not replace rendered previews.
Relations are editorial hypotheses; the visual review covers 12 concepts, not the whole corpus.
The ten-style fixture tests the entry; it does not describe a participant's real taste.

definitions.concept: A distinct expressive intent and content organization; distinctness needs editorial and visual confirmation.
definitions.variant: A different skin/fonts/radius on the same source screen.
definitions.layoutFamily: The existing COMPOSITIONS classification, separate from the content composition.
definitions.mediaRole: The role of the procedural image; its motif should not be carried into the layout automatically.
definitions.relation: An explainable editorial relation with limits and changed traits.

concepts.title: Typographic manifesto

legacyComposition.note: Centred headline and actions float alone in an open mesh field.

artDirection.intent: Express one strong promise through text scale and a central focal point.
artDirection.task: Quickly grasp the main claim and move to a single primary action.

composition.rationale: Central Stack: badge, text-8xl headline, lead and two buttons. The mesh fills the background without setting the reading order.
composition.mediaRole: An atmospheric mesh field behind the content; the background can change without rebuilding the central axis.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The primary tag matches the source markup; the mesh stays in the media layer.

invariants: Central axis and the order badge → title → lead → actions
Large headline scale relative to the explanation
The primary action and the secondary link are distinguishable
risks: A long headline can take up most of the frame
The background must keep text contrast
Radius shape has little effect on the overall structure

distinction.reason: Both are centered, but here there is a large claim, an explanation and a pair of actions; ref-c04 deliberately uses a small headline and one action.

concepts.title: Two-column dialogue

legacyComposition.note: Full-height media at the end plus a stats row along the foot of the text column.

artDirection.intent: Pair an explanation with an expressive image in two equal parts.
artDirection.task: Read the offer, look at the image and weigh the short proof points.
artDirection.focus: A large headline on the left tied to tall media on the right.

composition.rationale: Grid cols=2: title, lead, two buttons and stats on the left; a tall glass-panel on the right. The bottom stats row sits inside the text column.
composition.mediaRole: A glass panel with overlapping rectangles and glow; this is composition inside the image.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source L-arrangement has weak=true. Here the main principle is the balance of two parts; the source tag is kept separately.

invariants: Two large columns with independent roles
Stats after the actions in the text column
Media stays separate, not a text background
risks: The structure needs rethinking on a narrow screen
Media width and height affect the balance
Decorative glass does not explain the product's value

distinction.reason: Ref-c02 uses dense two columns and stats; ref-c12 links small masses through open space and a diagonal.

concepts.title: Full-width poster

legacyComposition.note: A media band across the top and a huge headline plus action row along the bottom.

artDirection.intent: Create a poster feel through a wide media band and an extremely large line.
artDirection.task: Take in the expressive claim, then the explanation and the action at the bottom edge.
artDirection.focus: A large-scale headline under a wide grainy field.

composition.rationale: Grain-band h-80 above a text-[168px] headline; below it, the lead on the left and the CTA on the right. Masses are stacked in horizontal layers.
composition.mediaRole: Grain is a standalone horizontal band; it is not a full-screen background.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source L-arrangement is kept as legacy; the refined principle describes a top band and a bottom base.

Poster-scale title
A bottom pairing of lead and CTA on opposite edges
risks: Long text changes the poster balance

concepts.title: Quiet center

legacyComposition.note: A small centred headline and button in a mostly empty screen; dots fade in from a corner.

artDirection.intent: Lower the visual pressure: a small message and one action inside a large open field.
artDirection.task: Quickly grasp a short claim and pick the single next step.
artDirection.focus: A small central headline and a single action.

composition.rationale: Central Stack with eyebrow, text-5xl title and an outline button. No lead and no second primary button.
composition.mediaRole: Dots fill the background; the corner motif is not carried into the content composition tag.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source secondary=diagonal refers to the corner dots field. The content composition records a central focal point.

invariants: Large open field
Small text scale relative to the frame
One primary action
risks: A complex offer does not fit the short form
Sparse information can feel empty
Extra CTAs would break the original clarity

distinction.reason: The quiet center is symmetric; the diagonal pause places text and image in different corners.

concepts.title: Claim and proof

legacyComposition.note: Headline takes two thirds, a square plate the last third, then a ruled row of four figures.

artDirection.intent: Join the main claim to a readable band of numeric proof points.
artDirection.task: Understand the offer and quickly assess a few key metrics.
artDirection.focus: A 2/3 text mass, then a separate row of metrics.

composition.rationale: Grid cols=3: text col-span-2, a square Flat in the remaining third; below, a Separator and Grid cols=4 with stats.
composition.mediaRole: Flat shapes fill the right third; the geometry inside it is secondary to the ratio of the large parts.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: Thirds are confirmed by col-span-2 in a three-column Grid. Stats are described separately from the composition tag.

invariants: A 2:1 ratio of the upper parts
A separate bottom band of stats
Metrics visually set apart from the hero
risks: The fixture repeats the first stat as the fourth, so these are not four different proof points
Numbers need context and a source in a real product
Extra metrics can overload the bottom

distinction.reason: Here metrics sit in a separate band; in the bento, information is spread across cards within a shared grid.

concepts.title: Editorial spread

legacyComposition.note: A 3/5/4 twelve-column spread: lead column, headline, tall picture; near thirds.

artDirection.intent: Offer several entry points into the content through typographic hierarchy, numbers and a separate image.
artDirection.task: Scan the topics, read the main piece and choose the next action.
artDirection.focus: A large headline in the middle column, supported by neighboring pieces.

composition.rationale: 12-column Grid: items col-span-3, headline/lead/action col-span-5, Duotone col-span-4. The central text is bottom-aligned.
composition.mediaRole: A tall Duotone v=1 is a procedural landscape, separate from the list and the text.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source rule-of-thirds is an approximation. Here the confirmed 3:5:4 proportions and editorial columns are recorded.

invariants: Three 3:5:4 columns with different roles
A numbered list of standalone entry points
A rule after the masthead and a bottom base for the main text
risks: A complex spread needs a clear order on a narrow screen
A visually large headline should not hide the meaning of the list
3:5:4 should not be treated as exact thirds

distinction.reason: Each column has a different role; ref-c03 builds one vertical poster story.

artDirection.intent: Explain the offer and give a concrete image of the result in a large frame.

composition.differenceFromLegacy: The primary pyramid is kept; radial describes the Conic inside the window, not the overall page structure.

composition.rationale: Two Geometric bands at the edges; the mx-60 middle column holds title, lead, Input+Button and TopicChips.
composition.mediaRole: The geometric edges act as frames around the work area.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The primary focal-mass is kept; the side geometric bands count as media. t009, removed from the panorama, is not used.

concepts.title: Hierarchical bento

legacyComposition.note: Bento: the two large tiles take two of three rows, small tiles the last row.

artDirection.intent: Gather varied content into a shared grid with two large areas and a small bottom row.
artDirection.task: Take in the main claim and quickly scan the supporting metrics.
artDirection.focus: A large text block on the left; media of equal area on the right.

composition.rationale: Grid cols=4, rows=3: hero col-span-2 row-span-2 and a Geometric of the same area; the bottom row has three stats and an info Card.
composition.mediaRole: Geometric is a large standalone grid area, not the layout of all blocks.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source rule-of-thirds refers to two of three rows vertically. The catalog uses the more precise modular-hierarchy and notes the 1:1 upper masses.

invariants: Large upper areas are separated from small bottom cards
All elements snap to the shared grid
Cell size signals relative importance
risks: The upper areas split the width in half, not in thirds
Equal hero and media size can create competing focal points
More cards shift the priorities

distinction.reason: Here there are two large masses and a small bottom row; ref-c11 has nine cells with the focal point in the center.

concepts.title: Center and surroundings

legacyComposition.note: Headline in the centre with figure and copy tiles on the four edges, conic plates in the corners.

artDirection.intent: Organize a rich field around a central message, using the surroundings as support.
artDirection.task: First find the main claim, then explore the neighboring blocks.
artDirection.focus: An accented central cell, supported by vertical and horizontal axes.

composition.rationale: Grid cols=3, rows=3: a central primary Card with title/action, stats above/below, text left/right, Conic in the four corners.
composition.mediaRole: Four Conic fields sit in the corners; the radial motif of each does not make the whole grid radial.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The source cross is confirmed by the central title and four edge cells; Conic is moved to media.

invariants: The main cell stays in the center
Four orthogonal neighbors support the center
Corner media does not compete with the message
risks: Bright corners can pull attention away from the center
A long title must fit the small central card
The grid needs its own reading order on a narrow screen

distinction.reason: The difference lies in geometry and priority: a central cell instead of a large side hero.

concepts.title: Diagonal pause

legacyComposition.note: Headline high at the start, picture square low at the end, one button between.

artDirection.intent: Create calm tension between small text at the start and a separate image in the opposite corner.
artDirection.task: Read a short message and look at the image while keeping a sense of open space.
artDirection.focus: The relation between the upper text mass and the lower-right image.

composition.rationale: Title/c.accent/Button in a Stack at the top start; Duotone size-80 as an absolute block at right-16 bottom-16.
composition.mediaRole: A small Duotone v=0 uses a placeholder MediaFrame; the frame shape alone does not define the diagonal.
composition.differenceFromLegacy: The primary diagonal is confirmed by block placement, not by the image's tilt or color.

invariants: Text and image occupy different corners
A large open field between the masses
Text stays small relative to the screen
risks: The image's absolute position can overlap long text
The c.accent value is not a full lead
The composition should not make the user hunt for the button

distinction.reason: Both are airy, but the symmetric center is replaced by a diagonal link between two masses.

scenarios.title: Choose a direction
